list.name: RoboRally: The Factory Rescue
list.description: A 3D maze game with no manual controls — players type natural-language missions, an AI agent plans the moves, a rules engine validates them, and the robot executes valid plans step by step.

details.overview: RoboRally: The Factory Rescue is a 3D maze game built for the Meta Global AI Developer Hackathon. There are no manual controls: players type natural-language missions, Meta Muse Spark 1.3 plans the moves in bounded segments, a rules engine validates every move, and the robot executes valid plans step by step in a real game engine. The project spans both hackathon themes: agent-driven machine control and natural-language robot operation. Built with Muse Code.
details.problem: Letting an AI agent directly control a robot is risky: unconstrained model output can ignore walls, hazards, and game physics, or declare success without earning it. The challenge was to give players natural-language control while keeping the game engine authoritative, so the AI can never bypass physics.
details.solution: Built an agentic loop of Mission, Plan, Validate, Execute, Observe, and replan. The model produces bounded plan segments of at most 12 moves, chained server-side, as constrained JSON; a server-side rules engine validates walls, lasers, doors, triggers, enemies, and battery; and the robot executes at 450 ms per step, stopping honestly on death, victory, or state change. Geometry is always server-loaded and community attempts are resimulated, so clients stay untrusted.
features: 🤖 Natural-language missions planned by Meta Muse Spark 1.3 with constrained JSON output.
🛡️ Server-side rules engine validating walls, lasers, doors, triggers, enemies, and battery.
🧩 6 hand-designed levels up to a 37-move finale, all verified solvable by automated guards.
🌐 Community platform with validated UGC levels, immutable versions, and per-level leaderboards.
🎓 Learning lab teaching BFS, Dijkstra, and A* through narrated search traces.
⚡ Real-time 3D execution in Three.js at 450 ms per step with honest stop conditions.
challenges: Constraining open-ended model output into bounded, valid move segments the engine could trust.
Keeping the game engine authoritative while still allowing fluid natural-language control.
Designing 6 levels that are challenging but provably solvable, verified by automated maze guards.
Hardening the setup documentation so a judge cloning the repo can run everything from the README alone.
lessons: Learned to design agentic loops where the model proposes and a deterministic engine disposes.
Gained experience with constrained structured output and tiered token budgets for AI agents.
Learned the value of judge-readiness: fresh-clone setup, fail-fast configuration, and troubleshooting docs.
Improved my ability to validate AI behavior with automated guards, including mission fuzz testing.

list.name: SignalBait
list.description: An AI-assisted phishing and scam message scanner that helps users identify suspicious messages and report potential threats.

details.overview: SignalBait is a full-stack web application designed to help users analyze potentially malicious messages and report suspicious activity. It combines a Vue.js frontend, a Spring Boot REST API, and a Python-based machine learning service. The analysis pipeline integrates the third-party facebook/bart-large-mnli model through Hugging Face Transformers for zero-shot text classification. The model is one component of the analysis pipeline and is not a model developed or trained by me.
details.problem: Phishing and scam messages can imitate legitimate communications, making them difficult for users to recognize. Users also need a straightforward way to report suspicious messages and follow up on reported issues.
details.solution: Built an AI-assisted scanning workflow, a ticket reporting system, and a ticket-tracking feature. Integrated facebook/bart-large-mnli as a third-party classifier through Hugging Face Transformers rather than claiming ownership of the model. The application uses Spring Boot for its main REST API and FastAPI for the Python-based analysis service.
features: 🔎 Analyze suspicious messages using an AI-assisted classification pipeline.
🖼️ Support both text and image input for message analysis.
🎯 Integrate the third-party facebook/bart-large-mnli model for zero-shot text classification.
🎫 Submit reports and receive a ticket number for follow-up.
📨 Receive email notifications about ticket creation and status changes.
🔍 Track reported tickets using a ticket number and reporter email.
🔐 Separate the scanning experience from the administrative ticket-management interface.
challenges: eparated ticket management and business logic into a Spring Boot backend while delegating AI/ML inference to a dedicated FastAPI service, enabling clear service responsibilities.
Connecting the Vue.js frontend to backend REST APIs and resolving cross-origin resource sharing (CORS) issues.
Coordinating ticket creation, tracking, and status notifications across application components.
Configuring environment variables and deployment settings for separate frontend and backend services.
Understanding the limitations of zero-shot classification and avoiding treating one model's output as a definitive security verdict.
lessons: Learned to integrate an existing third-party machine learning model without misrepresenting it as my own work.
Gained experience building and connecting REST APIs across Java and Python services.
Improved my understanding of environment-based configuration, CORS, and deployment troubleshooting.
Learned to distinguish between model predictions and definitive security conclusions.
Practiced designing a reporting workflow that supports ticket tracking and administrative follow-up.

list.name: SignalBait Admin Dashboard
list.description: An administrative dashboard for managing user reports, monitoring ticket statuses, viewing analytics, and reviewing audit logs.

details.overview: SignalBait Admin Dashboard is a separate administrative application for managing reports submitted through SignalBait. It provides an interface for reviewing tickets, updating their statuses, monitoring analytics, and inspecting audit logs. The frontend uses Angular and ECharts, while the backend uses Django. Both the dashboard and the main application work with the shared PostgreSQL database.
details.problem: Incoming reports need an organized management interface so administrators can review reported issues, update their progress, and monitor activity without relying on manual database operations.
details.solution: Developed an administrative dashboard with session-based authentication, ticket management, analytics visualizations, and audit-log viewing. The Angular frontend communicates with Django REST endpoints, while the backend accesses the shared PostgreSQL database used by the main application.
features: 🔐 Secure administrator login using session-based authentication.
🎫 View and manage reported tickets.
🔄 Update ticket statuses, including new, in-progress, and resolved.
📊 Visualize ticket statistics and trends using ECharts.
📋 Review audit logs to inspect administrative actions.
🗑️ Delete tickets when administrative action is required.
challenges: Implementing session-based authentication and handling cross-origin requests with credentials.
Keeping ticket fields and data types consistent between Django models and the existing PostgreSQL schema.
Coordinating ticket updates with the main application's ticket-tracking and email-notification workflow.
Separating frontend and backend deployment configuration while maintaining communication between services.
lessons: Learned to build an administrative frontend with Angular and TypeScript.
Gained experience developing backend endpoints with Django and Python.
Improved my understanding of session authentication, CORS, and credentialed HTTP requests.
Learned to integrate data visualization into an administrative interface using ECharts.
Gained practical experience coordinating a shared database across separate applications.

list.name: SignalBait Mobile
list.description: An Android mobile application that extends SignalBait's AI-assisted message scanning and ticket-management capabilities to mobile devices.

details.overview: SignalBait Mobile is the Android companion to SignalBait, a full-stack message-scanning platform designed to help users assess potentially malicious messages and report issues with analysis results. Built with Flutter and Dart, the mobile application connects to separate FastAPI and Spring Boot backend services for message analysis and ticket management, respectively.
details.problem: The existing SignalBait experience was web-based. I wanted to extend its core functionality to Android while gaining practical experience in mobile application development and cross-platform UI frameworks.
details.solution: Developed an Android mobile application using Flutter and Dart, integrating the existing FastAPI scanning service and Spring Boot ticket-management API. The app supports text and image analysis, issue reporting, ticket tracking, and access to security guidance without requiring a separate mobile backend.
features: 🔎 Analyze potentially suspicious messages through the existing AI-assisted scanning service.
🖼️ Submit text or images for message analysis.
🎯 Use a third-party facebook/bart-large-mnli model through Hugging Face Transformers for zero-shot classification in the scanning backend.
🎫 Submit reports about incorrect analysis results and receive a ticket number.
📨 Receive email notifications related to ticket creation and status changes through the ticketing service.
🔍 Track reported tickets using a ticket number and reporter email.
📱 Access scanning, ticket management, and FAQ guidance through an Android-focused mobile interface.
challenges: Integrating the Flutter application with two independent REST APIs built using different backend technologies.
Handling text and image submissions to the FastAPI scanning service.
Coordinating ticket submission and tracking with the Spring Boot backend.
Configuring Android networking and troubleshooting differences between emulator and physical-device environments.
Understanding the limitations of zero-shot classification and presenting model outputs as risk indicators rather than definitive security verdicts.
lessons: Gained practical experience developing Android applications with Flutter and Dart.
Learned to integrate existing backend services into a mobile application without duplicating backend functionality.
Improved my understanding of HTTP requests, API error handling, and mobile networking.
Learned to distinguish between model predictions and definitive security conclusions.
Practiced extending an existing full-stack project to a new platform while maintaining separate service responsibilities.

list.name: Urgent or Is It?
list.description: A spiritual successor to Phish or Miss, Urgent or Is It? provides players with a lore-rich and educational experience focused on identifying phishing attempts.

details.overview: A full-stack web-based cybersecurity awareness game built with Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS on the frontend, with a NestJS and MongoDB backend. The application uses JWT-based authentication to manage user sessions, profiles, and persistent game progression.
details.problem: After developing Phish or Miss, I realized that I wanted to expand beyond my existing Flask and React experience and build a more complete full-stack application using a broader modern technology stack. This project became an opportunity to strengthen my frontend, backend, database, authentication, deployment, and CI/CD skills while creating a spiritual successor to Phish or Miss.
details.solution: I rebuilt the concept from the ground up using a modern full-stack architecture with Next.js, React, TypeScript, NestJS, and MongoDB. The application includes persistent player progression, user authentication, protected backend endpoints, and interactive phishing-detection scenarios. I also introduced automated CI/CD workflows with GitHub Actions and deployed the application using separate frontend and backend services.
features: 🎭 Lore-rich phishing scenarios designed to make cybersecurity awareness more engaging.
🎯 Interactive gameplay focused on identifying phishing attempts.
👤 User registration, authentication, and player profiles.
💾 Persistent per-user game progression stored in MongoDB.
🔐 JWT-based authentication with bcrypt password hashing.
🛡️ Protected API endpoints with NestJS guards and DTO-based validation.
🌐 RESTful API architecture connecting the frontend and backend.
⚙️ Automated CI/CD workflows using GitHub Actions.
☁️ Deployed frontend and backend services using Vercel.
challenges: Expanding beyond my previous Flask-based backend experience and learning NestJS for a new full-stack architecture.
Migrating from primarily JavaScript-based development toward a fully TypeScript-based application.
Designing a clean separation between the Next.js frontend and NestJS backend.
Implementing authentication, authorization, password hashing, and protected API endpoints securely.
Designing MongoDB schemas and persistent game-state storage for individual players.
Configuring frontend-to-backend communication across separately deployed services.
Setting up automated CI/CD workflows and deployment with GitHub Actions.
lessons: Learned that expanding my breadth across the stack is important for becoming a more versatile software engineer.
Strengthened my understanding of TypeScript and modern React/Next.js development.
Gained practical experience building backend services with NestJS and Mongoose.
Deepened my understanding of authentication, authorization, password hashing, and API security.
Learned how frontend, backend, database, deployment, and CI/CD concerns fit together in a complete application.
Improved my ability to independently learn unfamiliar technologies and integrate them into a working system.
Realized that building an application from scratch is an effective way to identify gaps in my technical breadth and deliberately address them.

list.name: Portfolio Website
list.description: Modern multilingual portfolio website built with Next.js and TypeScript to showcase my projects, technical skills, and my academic and professional journey.

details.overview: A complete redesign of my original portfolio, developed using Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. The website serves as both a professional portfolio and a demonstration of modern frontend engineering practices, featuring reusable components, multilingual support, responsive layouts, dark mode, and interactive project showcases.
details.problem: My previous portfolio reached the end of the AWS Free Tier. Rather than simply migrating the existing website, I took the opportunity to evaluate its architecture and user experience. I realized there were several aspects that could be improved, including maintainability, scalability, multilingual support, responsiveness, and the way projects were presented to recruiters.
details.solution: I rebuilt the portfolio from scratch using Next.js App Router, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS. The new architecture emphasizes reusable components, JSON-driven localization, responsive design, and interactive project modals with screenshot carousels. The result is a cleaner, more maintainable codebase that can continue evolving alongside my skills and future projects.
features: 🌍 Multilingual interface supporting English, Indonesian, Japanese, and Chinese.
🌙 Light and dark mode with system preference detection.
📱 Responsive design optimized for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.
🗂️ Interactive project cards with detailed project modals.
🖼️ Screenshot carousel for showcasing project interfaces.
⚡ JSON-based content management for scalable localization.
🎨 Modern UI built with reusable React components and Tailwind CSS.
challenges: Migrating from JavaScript to a fully TypeScript-based codebase.
Designing reusable components that remain maintainable as the portfolio grows.
Building a scalable internationalization system using JSON dictionaries.
Managing complex component interactions such as project modals and screenshot carousels.
Balancing aesthetics, performance, accessibility, and responsiveness across different devices.
lessons: Strengthened my understanding of modern React, Next.js, and TypeScript development.
Learned the value of planning component architecture before implementation.
Developed practical experience building scalable multilingual applications.
Improved my frontend UI/UX design process through continuous iteration and refinement.
Realized that rebuilding a project from scratch can sometimes be more effective than continuously patching an existing codebase.

list.name: TreeVisual
list.description: Offline desktop application that visualizes binary tree operations to help students learn Data Structures and Algorithms.

details.overview: TreeVisual is a lightweight desktop application designed to help students understand binary trees through interactive visualization. Built with PySide6, it provides an offline learning environment for practicing common binary tree operations without requiring an internet connection.
details.problem: Many binary tree visualizers available online require an internet connection or provide limited interactivity. In addition, developing the application required learning PySide6, a GUI framework that I had not previously worked with, while designing an intuitive educational interface.
details.solution: Developed a lightweight offline desktop application that enables users to interactively visualize binary tree operations. The application focuses on simplicity, responsiveness, and accessibility, making it suitable for students learning Data Structures and Algorithms.
features: 🌳 Interactive visualization of binary tree structures.
➕ Insert new nodes dynamically.
❌ Delete existing nodes while updating the visualization.
🔍 Search for nodes within the tree.
🔄 Visualize tree traversals (Preorder, Inorder, and Postorder).
💻 Fully offline desktop application with no internet dependency.
challenges: Ensuring insertion, deletion, and traversal algorithms behaved correctly across different tree structures.
Synchronizing the graphical visualization with the underlying binary tree data structure.
Learning PySide6 while developing a responsive and intuitive desktop user interface.
lessons: Learned desktop application development using the PySide6 framework.
Strengthened my understanding of binary tree algorithms and data structures.
Improved my ability to design educational software with a clear and intuitive user experience.
Gained experience translating algorithmic concepts into interactive visualizations.

list.name: Phish or Miss
list.description: Hackathon project that teaches users to recognize phishing emails and messages through interactive gameplay in a safe learning environment.

details.overview: Phish or Miss is an educational web application developed during the NTUxBase3 Hackathon. The game challenges players to identify phishing emails and messages through realistic scenarios, helping them develop awareness of common social engineering techniques in an engaging and risk-free environment.
details.problem: The hackathon challenged participants to build a real-world solution using the Sogni SDK. Although generative AI has enormous creative potential, many users still lack access to engaging and educational AI-powered experiences outside centralized, subscription-based platforms.
details.solution: I developed an interactive web-based game that presents users with realistic email and messaging scenarios, encouraging them to distinguish legitimate communications from phishing attempts. Immediate feedback helps reinforce cybersecurity awareness while keeping the learning experience engaging.
features: 📧 Interactive phishing email detection game.
💬 Simulated phishing message scenarios inspired by real-world attacks.
✅ Immediate feedback with explanations after each decision.
🎮 Gamified learning experience designed to improve cybersecurity awareness.
☁️ Cloud-hosted application deployed using AWS EC2.
challenges: Designing phishing scenarios that realistically reflected modern social engineering attacks.
Completing the entire project independently within the five-day hackathon deadline.
Integrating the Sogni SDK into a cohesive web application.
Balancing educational value with engaging gameplay.
lessons: Developed a deeper understanding of how social engineering exploits human psychology rather than technical vulnerabilities.
Strengthened rapid prototyping and time management skills under hackathon constraints.
Gained experience integrating third-party SDKs into a full-stack web application.
Learned the importance of clear user feedback when designing educational cybersecurity tools.

list.name: Legacy Portfolio Website
list.description: My first personal portfolio website built with React and deployed on AWS, marking my transition from Python-based web development to modern frontend development. This project ultimately inspired the complete redesign and redevelopment of my current portfolio using Next.js, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.

details.overview: My first portfolio website designed to showcase my projects and technical skills. The project marked my transition from Python-based web development to React while introducing me to cloud deployment using AWS services.
details.problem: The original portfolio was hosted on Render using Flask. While functional, Render's free tier required visitors to wait for the application to wake up, resulting in a poor user experience. At the same time, I wanted practical experience with AWS while preparing for the AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner certification.
details.solution: Rebuilt the frontend using React and migrated the deployment to AWS using Amazon S3 for static hosting and CloudFront as a global CDN. This significantly improved loading times and provided hands-on experience with modern frontend deployment.
features: 🌐 Responsive portfolio website.
📁 Project showcase section.
👨‍💻 About Me section.
📞 Contact information.
☁️ Static website deployment using AWS S3 and CloudFront.
challenges: Learning React after previously developing primarily with Flask.
Migrating from a server-rendered architecture to a client-side React application.
Configuring AWS S3 and CloudFront for static website hosting.
Designing a portfolio that balanced simplicity with professionalism.
lessons: Built a strong foundation in React component-based development.
Gained practical experience deploying static web applications on AWS.
Learned how CDN-based deployment improves website performance.
Established the foundation and design principles that inspired my current portfolio.

list.name: AI-NTeractive
list.description: Final Year Project that leverages neural networks and facial animation technology to create a more engaging learning experience.

details.overview: AI-NTeractive is an AI-powered Learning Management System (LMS) developed as our Final Year Project. The platform integrates neural networks and facial animation technology to make online learning more engaging through interactive, animated educational content.
details.problem: Traditional Learning Management Systems often rely on static text and videos, which can reduce student engagement. Our challenge was to integrate SadTalker facial animation technology into a practical educational platform while ensuring the system remained intuitive, scalable, and useful for both students and educators.
details.solution: We designed and developed an AI-enhanced LMS that combines conventional learning management features with AI-generated facial animations. As Team Leader, I coordinated development, delegated tasks, managed project milestones, and ensured successful integration between the web platform, database, and AI services.
features: 💬 Face-Animated AI Assistant – Provides personalized responses using expressive facial animations.
🎬 Video Creation Studio – Allows educators to generate AI-assisted educational videos.
🏫 Interactive Classroom – Centralizes animated learning materials to improve engagement.
👥 User Authentication – Secure login and role-based access for students and instructors.
☁️ Cloud Deployment – Hosted using Google Cloud services.
challenges: Integrating SadTalker with the web application while maintaining acceptable response times.
Coordinating development across a five-member multidisciplinary team.
Balancing AI processing workloads with overall application performance.
Ensuring generated animations remained relevant and suitable for educational use.
lessons: Learned how to integrate AI services into a production-oriented web application.
Strengthened leadership and project management skills by coordinating a five-member team.
Gained experience deploying and maintaining cloud-based applications.
Developed a deeper understanding of machine learning integration within full-stack systems.

list.name: Car Loaning System
list.description: Web-based platform for managing the lifecycle of used car transactions with role-based access control.

details.overview: A web-based platform developed to manage the complete lifecycle of used car transactions. The system supports multiple user roles—including administrators, agents, buyers, and sellers—with role-based access control and dedicated workflows for each user type.
details.problem: The project was required to follow the Boundary-Control-Entity (BCE) architectural pattern as part of the course requirements. As Scrum Team Lead, I was also responsible for coordinating a seven-member team with varying technical backgrounds while ensuring consistent code quality and up-to-date project documentation.
details.solution: Adopted the Scrum framework with regular sprint planning, stand-up meetings, and task allocation to organize development. Responsibilities were divided according to each member's strengths, while continuous reviews ensured compliance with the BCE architecture and project milestones.
features: 🛠️ Administrator Dashboard – Manage user accounts and system administration.
🚗 Agent Dashboard – Create, update, and manage vehicle listings while reviewing buyer feedback.
👤 Buyer Portal – Browse available vehicles, submit reviews, and manage purchase requests.
🧾 Seller Portal – Submit vehicle information through agents and monitor customer feedback.
🔐 Role-Based Access Control – Different interfaces and permissions for each user role.
challenges: Designing the application to comply with the Boundary-Control-Entity (BCE) architecture.
Coordinating development across a seven-member Scrum team with different skill levels.
Maintaining consistent documentation alongside rapid feature development.
Integrating multiple user workflows into a cohesive system.
lessons: Gained practical experience leading a Scrum team through a complete software development lifecycle.
Learned how software architecture decisions influence maintainability and scalability.
Improved communication, task delegation, and project planning skills.
Developed a stronger appreciation for documentation as part of professional software engineering.
